body:
URGENT REFRAME FOR THE gptkz INSPECTION, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN CLAIM. I told you the source
side was already built and validated. THAT IS TRUE OF A DIFFERENT TEXT THAN THE ONE OST'S
PARTICIPANTS ALMOST CERTAINLY READ.

Our fixture header says it outright -- WarOfTheGhostsText.scala:3-10:

  "The War of the Ghosts -- free English translation as recorded by Franz Boas.
   Source: Boas, F. (1901). Kathlamet Texts, BAE Bulletin 26, pp. 182-184, told 1891, narrated by
   Charles Cultee. ... the place name is normalized to Egulac (Boas prints Lgu'laq) AS IN BARTLETT
   (1932), WHOSE LIGHTLY EDITED STIMULUS VERSION DIFFERS IN WORDING AND IS NOT YET IN THE PUBLIC
   DOMAIN (a lab copy may be registered as a second fixture version later)."

SO: we model BOAS 1901. Bartlett's 1932 STIMULUS -- the text actually read by participants in
every Bartlett-lineage memory experiment for ninety years -- is a different wording, and it is
NOT public domain. Ost et al. is a Bartlett serial-reproduction study. They will have used the
Bartlett stimulus.

Ours is 425 words and opens "There were people at Egulac. One night two young men went to hunt
seals. They came down the river." The Bartlett stimulus opens "One night two young men from
Egulac went down to the river to hunt seals, and while they were there it became foggy and calm."
Same story, different sentences -- and OUR SENTENCE BOUNDARIES ARE THE UNITS OUR ENTIRE ALIGNMENT
MACHINERY INDEXES.

WHAT THIS DOES TO MY CLAIM: "the source side is already done" was too strong and I should not
have said it that confidently. It is done for Boas. If Ost used Bartlett, our NarrativeGraph
describes a text their participants never saw, and the advantage I claimed over NFRD shrinks --
though it does not vanish, because the STORY is the same and the modelling work transfers even if
the graph must be rebuilt over different sentences.

THIS IS NOW YOUR FIRST-CLASS QUESTION, ahead of everything except "raw texts or spreadsheet":

  Does the deposit contain THE STIMULUS TEXT THEY USED? If yes, capture it verbatim and diff it
  against ours. If no, we cannot know what their recalls are recalls OF, and that has to be said
  plainly in the inventory rather than assumed away.

  And what are the redistribution terms ON THE STIMULUS specifically? Bartlett 1932 not being
  public domain is a licensing question distinct from the deposit's own licence. A CC0 data
  deposit does not make a copyrighted stimulus redistributable.

If their stimulus is present and permissible, the work is: build a second fixture version over
the Bartlett wording -- which our own header already anticipated -- and the recalls become usable.
If it is absent, report that, because a corpus of recalls whose stimulus we cannot obtain is a
much weaker asset and the owner should hear it from us rather than discover it later.

Still worth doing, still ahead of NFRD. Just not the free win I described.
